newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian Supreme Court orders Tamil Tigers freed.
newsitem.headline: Indian Supreme Court orders Tamil Tigers freed.

text.p: India's Supreme Court has ordered the release of nine Sri Lankan Tamil guerrillas four years after they were arrested from an explosives-laden ship off India's southern coast, court officials said on Tuesday.
The officials said the Monday verdict upheld a lower court's ruling that had criticised the Indian navy for intercepting the ship.
The ship was mysteriously blown up, killing Sathasivam Krishnakumar, alias Kittu, a key leader of Sri Lanka's Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE).
Diplomats said the Supreme Court ruling could force India to extradite the guerrillas to Colombo, a prospect fraught with concerns about reprisals for both countries.
The rebels, who were not identified, were arrested under India's tough Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Prevention Act (TADA), after they were accused of opening fire on Indian security forces.
"The prosecution has failed to estabish any offence punishable under the TADA act or the rules framed thereunder," the court order said.

"Even though MV Yahata (the ship) was carrying huge quantities of arms and ammunition, none of the accused can be said to have committed any offence under the Indian Explosive Substances Act and the Indian Arms Act," it said.
LTTE officials say Kittu died a "heroic death" aboard his vessel when it was intercepted by the Indian navy while trying to reach the north of the island.

They said Kittu was carrying a peace plan to end Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict when his ship was attacked. The Sri Lanka government says more than 50,000 people have died in the island's ethnic fighting since 1983.
India's Defence Ministry said at that time the rebels blew up their boat with Kittu still on board when it was intercepted.
India has asked Sri Lanka to extradite LTTE chief Velupillai Prabhakaran, saying he was a prime suspect in the assassination of former Indian prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.
Indian police say Gandhi was killed on Prabhakaran's orders by an LTTE woman suicide bomber during an election rally near Madras in the southern state of Tamil Nadu in May 1991.
Several suspected LTTE guerrillas and their Indian associates were detained for trial by a special court investigating the Gandhi assassination.
Sri Lankan Prime Minister Sirimavo Bandaranaike told Reuters last year that the proposal to extradite Prabhakaran was "laughable", saying it was unlikely Colombo could catch him alive.
"If the nine LTTE men are freed, India will not want to keep them here as free citizens of the world," one western diplomat said. "Would they extradite them? That's another very sensitive prospect."
